stem: How does the eye involvement in HLA-B27 associated arthritis differ from that seen in ANA-positive oligoarticular JIA?

options.text: It presents as an acute, red, and painful eye
It is entirely asymptomatic and requires screening
It only occurs in children under age 5
It never leads to long-term vision damage

explanation: In enthesitis-related or HLA-B27 associated arthritis, eye involvement (iritis) is symptomatic and clinical, whereas in ANA+ JIA, it is asymptomatic.
rationale: One form is a 'silent' disease, while the other is an 'acute' medical presentation.

optionExplanations.A: In enthesitis-related or HLA-B27 associated arthritis, eye involvement (iritis) is symptomatic and clinical, whereas in ANA+ JIA, it is asymptomatic.
optionExplanations.B: This describes the uveitis seen in ANA-positive JIA, not the acute iritis seen in spondyloarthropathies.
optionExplanations.C: Oligoarticular JIA often starts under age 5, but HLA-B27 associated conditions often present in older children and adults.
optionExplanations.D: Any form of intraocular inflammation, if untreated, can potentially cause damage, though the presentation differs.
